events.title: Jesus Ascends from the Mount of Olives
events.description: After appearing to the apostles for forty days, Jesus instructs them to await the Holy Spirit and commissions them as witnesses from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth. They watch him ascend and then return to Jerusalem in prayer.

events.title: Matthias Replaces Judas
events.description: Peter leads about one hundred twenty believers in choosing a replacement for Judas from among those who accompanied Jesus' ministry. After prayer and casting lots, Matthias is added to the eleven apostles.

events.title: The Holy Spirit Comes at Pentecost
events.description: At Pentecost the disciples are filled with the Holy Spirit and speak in languages understood by pilgrims from many nations. Peter explains the event through Israel's scriptures and proclaims Jesus' resurrection, after which about three thousand people are baptized.

events.title: The Jerusalem Community Shares Its Life
events.description: The growing community devotes itself to apostolic teaching, fellowship, shared meals, and prayer. Believers share possessions according to need, gather in the temple and homes, and continue gaining new members.

events.title: Peter Heals a Man at the Temple
events.description: Peter restores a man unable to walk since birth at the temple's Beautiful Gate. As a crowd gathers in amazement, Peter attributes the healing to Jesus and calls Israel to turn back to God.

events.title: Peter and John Testify before the Council
events.description: Temple authorities arrest Peter and John for proclaiming resurrection in Jesus. The council cannot deny the healed man's recovery, so it threatens the apostles and releases them, while the number of believing men has grown to about five thousand.

events.title: The Community Prays for Boldness
events.description: After hearing of the council's threats, the believers pray together and are filled anew with the Holy Spirit. Their common life includes generous distribution of property proceeds, exemplified by Barnabas's gift of a field.

events.title: Ananias and Sapphira Die after Deception
events.description: Ananias and Sapphira secretly retain part of a property's proceeds while presenting their gift as complete. Peter exposes their deception, and each dies in turn, bringing fear upon the whole church.

events.title: Apostolic Signs Draw Crowds
events.description: The apostles perform many signs among people gathered at Solomon's Portico. Growing crowds bring sick and tormented people from Jerusalem and neighboring towns, and all are healed.

events.title: The Apostles Are Freed and Flogged
events.description: The high priest has the apostles imprisoned, but an angel releases them to resume teaching in the temple. Brought again before the council, they escape execution after Gamaliel urges restraint, receive a flogging, and continue proclaiming Jesus.

events.title: Seven Are Appointed for the Daily Distribution
events.description: A complaint that Greek-speaking widows are neglected prompts the community to select seven Spirit-filled men to oversee the daily distribution. The apostles pray and lay hands on them while the Jerusalem movement continues to grow.

events.title: Stephen Is Tried and Stoned
events.description: Opponents seize Stephen and bring false testimony before the council. He recounts Israel's history, accuses his hearers of resisting God, sees a heavenly vision, and is stoned while Saul approves the killing.

events.title: Persecution Scatters the Jerusalem Believers
events.description: A severe persecution follows Stephen's death, scattering believers through Judea and Samaria while the apostles remain in Jerusalem. Saul enters homes, imprisons believers, and those dispersed carry the message into new places.

events.title: Philip Proclaims the Messiah in Samaria
events.description: Philip's preaching and signs bring many Samaritans to baptism, including the magician Simon. Peter and John come from Jerusalem and pray for the converts to receive the Holy Spirit, then rebuke Simon when he tries to buy apostolic power.

events.title: Philip Baptizes an Ethiopian Official
events.description: Directed to the Gaza road, Philip meets an Ethiopian court official reading Isaiah and explains the passage in relation to Jesus. He baptizes the traveler, is carried away by the Spirit, and continues preaching from Azotus to Caesarea.

events.title: Saul Encounters Jesus near Damascus
events.description: While traveling to arrest disciples in Damascus, Saul is struck blind by a heavenly encounter with Jesus. The disciple Ananias lays hands on him despite his fear, and Saul regains sight, receives the Holy Spirit, and is baptized.

events.title: Saul Preaches in Damascus and Jerusalem
events.description: Saul immediately proclaims Jesus in Damascus and escapes a plot against him by being lowered through the city wall. Barnabas introduces him to wary Jerusalem believers, and another threat leads the community to send him through Caesarea to Tarsus.

events.title: Peter Heals Aeneas and Raises Tabitha
events.description: At Lydda Peter heals Aeneas after eight years of paralysis. In Joppa he prays over the dead disciple Tabitha and restores her to life, leading many in the region to believe.

events.title: Cornelius and Peter Receive Coordinated Visions
events.description: An angel directs the Roman centurion Cornelius to summon Peter from Joppa. Meanwhile Peter sees a vision overturning distinctions of ritual impurity and is instructed to accompany the centurion's messengers without hesitation.

events.title: The Spirit Falls on Cornelius's Household
events.description: Peter enters Cornelius's Gentile household and announces God's impartial welcome through Jesus. The Holy Spirit falls on the listeners while Peter is speaking, and he orders them baptized.

events.title: Peter Defends the Gentile Baptisms
events.description: Jerusalem believers criticize Peter for eating with uncircumcised people. He recounts the visions and the Spirit's arrival, and the assembly concludes that God has granted life-giving repentance to Gentiles as well.

events.title: A Church Forms among Greeks at Antioch
events.description: Scattered believers proclaim Jesus to Greeks in Antioch, and Barnabas is sent to encourage the growing church. He brings Saul from Tarsus for a year of teaching, while the community also prepares famine relief for Judea after Agabus's warning.

events.title: Herod Kills James and Peter Escapes Prison
events.description: Herod Agrippa executes James son of Zebedee and arrests Peter during the festival season. An angel leads Peter past his guards, and he reaches believers praying at Mary's house before leaving for another place.

events.title: Herod Agrippa Dies at Caesarea
events.description: During a public address at Caesarea, Herod accepts divine acclaim from the crowd and is struck down. Barnabas and Saul complete their relief mission and return with John Mark as the movement continues to spread.

events.title: Antioch Sends Barnabas and Saul
events.description: While Antioch's prophets and teachers worship and fast, the Holy Spirit directs the church to set apart Barnabas and Saul. The community prays, lays hands on them, and sends them out.

events.title: The Mission Crosses Cyprus
events.description: Barnabas, Saul, and John Mark preach across Cyprus from Salamis to Paphos. Saul, now also called Paul, confronts the magician Elymas, whose temporary blindness contributes to the proconsul Sergius Paulus becoming a believer.

events.title: Paul Preaches at Pisidian Antioch
events.description: After John Mark leaves the mission at Perga, Paul and Barnabas enter Pisidian Antioch and address the synagogue. Their proclamation attracts much of the city, but opposition drives them onward after they announce a widening mission to Gentiles.

events.title: Division at Iconium Forces the Mission onward
events.description: Paul and Barnabas gain Jewish and Greek believers at Iconium and remain there as signs accompany their teaching. When a divided city turns toward violence and stoning, they escape into Lycaonia and continue preaching.

events.title: Paul Heals a Man and Is Stoned at Lystra
events.description: Paul heals a man unable to walk from birth, prompting the crowd to mistake him and Barnabas for gods and attempt sacrifice. Opponents later turn the crowd against Paul and stone him, but he rises and departs for Derbe.

events.title: Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch
events.description: After making disciples at Derbe, Paul and Barnabas retrace their route, strengthen the new churches, and appoint elders. They sail from Attalia to Syrian Antioch and report how their mission opened faith to Gentiles.

events.title: Jerusalem Affirms Gentile Inclusion
events.description: Disagreement over requiring circumcision brings Paul and Barnabas to meet the apostles and elders in Jerusalem. Peter, Paul, Barnabas, and James support welcoming Gentiles without imposing the full law, and a letter communicates limited communal requirements to Antioch.

events.title: Paul and Barnabas Begin Separate Journeys
events.description: A sharp disagreement over John Mark divides the former partners. Barnabas takes Mark to Cyprus, while Paul chooses Silas and travels through Syria and Cilicia strengthening churches.

events.title: Timothy Joins Paul and Silas
events.description: At Lystra Paul recruits the well-regarded disciple Timothy and has him circumcised in view of local Jewish communities. The travelers deliver Jerusalem's decisions and strengthen the churches.

events.title: A Vision Directs Paul toward Macedonia
events.description: Prevented from preaching in several regions of Asia Minor, the group reaches Troas. Paul's night vision of a Macedonian requesting help convinces them to cross into Europe.

events.title: Lydia and Her Household Are Baptized
events.description: At Philippi Paul speaks to women gathered for prayer beside the river. Lydia, a merchant from Thyatira, responds to the message, receives baptism with her household, and hosts the missionaries.

events.title: Paul and Silas Are Jailed at Philippi
events.description: After Paul frees an enslaved girl from a divining spirit, her owners have him and Silas beaten and imprisoned. An earthquake opens the prison, but they remain and prevent the jailer's suicide; he and his household are baptized before the magistrates apologize to the Roman citizens.

events.title: The Mission Faces Opposition in Macedonia
events.description: Paul's synagogue teaching gains adherents in Thessalonica, but a hostile crowd attacks Jason's house and forces the missionaries onward. Beroeans receive the message eagerly until opponents arrive from Thessalonica, prompting Paul's departure for Athens.

events.title: Paul Addresses the Areopagus
events.description: Distressed by Athens's many idols, Paul debates in its synagogue and marketplace and is brought before the Areopagus. He presents the creator as transcending human temples and calls for repentance in light of resurrection, winning a small group of believers.

events.title: Paul Establishes a Ministry in Corinth
events.description: Paul works with the recently displaced Aquila and Priscilla and teaches in Corinth for eighteen months. After synagogue opposition he focuses on Gentiles, while Crispus and many Corinthians believe and are baptized.

events.title: Gallio Dismisses the Case against Paul
events.description: Opponents bring Paul before Gallio's tribunal and accuse him over unlawful worship. The proconsul treats the dispute as an internal question of Jewish law and dismisses the case.

events.title: Paul Returns through Ephesus to Antioch
events.description: Paul leaves Corinth with Priscilla and Aquila, briefly teaches at Ephesus, and sails onward while promising to return if possible. After visiting Caesarea and Jerusalem, he reaches Antioch and later begins strengthening disciples through Galatia and Phrygia.

events.title: Priscilla and Aquila Instruct Apollos
events.description: The eloquent Alexandrian teacher Apollos arrives in Ephesus knowing only John's baptism. Priscilla and Aquila explain the movement more fully, and he then travels to Achaia and publicly argues that Jesus is the Messiah.

events.title: Paul Baptizes Twelve Disciples at Ephesus
events.description: At Ephesus Paul meets about twelve disciples acquainted only with John's baptism. They are baptized in Jesus' name and receive the Holy Spirit when Paul lays hands on them.

events.title: Paul Teaches throughout His Ephesian Ministry
events.description: Paul first teaches in the synagogue and then spends two years in the lecture hall of Tyrannus, allowing the message to spread across Asia. Extraordinary healings, a failed imitation by Sceva's sons, and a public burning of magical books mark the ministry's impact.

events.title: The Ephesian Theater Erupts over Artemis
events.description: Silversmiths fearing loss of trade stir a crowd in defense of Artemis and drag Paul's companions into the theater. Friends prevent Paul from entering, and the town clerk disperses the assembly by directing complaints toward the courts.

events.title: Paul Travels through Macedonia and Greece
events.description: Paul leaves Ephesus, encourages believers through Macedonia, and spends three months in Greece. A plot changes his planned voyage to Syria, so he returns through Macedonia with representatives from several churches.

events.title: Eutychus Is Restored at Troas
events.description: During an extended nighttime meeting at Troas, the young Eutychus falls asleep at a window and drops three stories. Paul embraces him and restores him alive before continuing the gathering until dawn.

events.title: Paul Bids Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
events.description: Hurrying toward Jerusalem, Paul summons the Ephesian elders to Miletus. He reviews his ministry, warns of future dangers, entrusts them with care of the church, and shares an emotional farewell.

events.title: Warnings Accompany Paul's Journey to Jerusalem
events.description: Paul's party sails along the eastern Mediterranean toward Jerusalem. Disciples at Tyre warn him, and at Caesarea Agabus symbolically predicts his arrest, but Paul continues despite his companions' pleas.

events.title: Paul Meets James and Enters Purification
events.description: Jerusalem's elders welcome Paul's report of his Gentile ministry but describe rumors that he rejects Jewish customs. At their advice he joins four men completing vows and enters the temple purification rites.

events.title: A Temple Crowd Attacks Paul
events.description: Jews from Asia accuse Paul of teaching against Israel and falsely suppose he brought a Gentile into the temple. A Roman tribune rescues him from the violent crowd, arrests him, and permits him to address the people from the barracks steps.

events.title: Paul Defends His Mission to the Crowd
events.description: Paul recounts his former persecution, encounter near Damascus, and commission to Gentiles. The crowd erupts at the mention of Gentiles, but Paul avoids examination by flogging when he reveals his Roman citizenship.

events.title: Paul Divides the Council over Resurrection
events.description: Before the council, Paul identifies his hope in resurrection as the issue, provoking conflict between Pharisees and Sadducees. Soldiers remove him from the violence, and that night he receives assurance that he will also testify in Rome.

events.title: A Murder Plot Sends Paul to Caesarea
events.description: More than forty conspirators plan to ambush and kill Paul, but his nephew reports the plot to the Roman tribune. A large escort transfers Paul by night to Governor Felix at Caesarea.

events.title: Paul Answers His Accusers before Felix
events.description: The attorney Tertullus accuses Paul of sedition and temple profanation, while Paul denies stirring any disturbance and locates the dispute in resurrection hope. Felix postpones judgment and repeatedly summons Paul while hoping for a bribe.

events.title: Felix Leaves Paul Imprisoned for Two Years
events.description: Paul remains in Caesarean custody for two years. When Porcius Festus succeeds Felix, the outgoing governor leaves Paul imprisoned as a concession to Judean leaders.

events.title: Paul Appeals to the Emperor
events.description: Festus hears renewed charges against Paul and proposes a Jerusalem trial. Paul invokes his right as a Roman citizen to appeal to the emperor, and Festus agrees to send him.

events.title: Paul Testifies before Agrippa
events.description: Festus presents Paul's unresolved case to Agrippa and Bernice before sending him to Rome. Paul recounts his calling and resurrection hope; Agrippa and the officials conclude that he has done nothing deserving imprisonment or death.

events.title: Paul's Voyage Is Driven across the Mediterranean
events.description: Paul sails for Italy under the centurion Julius, but the ship leaves Crete too late in the season and is caught in a violent northeaster. After fourteen days adrift, Paul reports divine assurance that all aboard will survive and encourages the passengers to eat.

events.title: The Ship Wrecks on Malta
events.description: The vessel runs aground and breaks apart, yet all 276 people reach Malta alive. Paul survives a viper bite, heals the father of the island's leading man, and cures other sick residents during the three-month stay.

events.title: Paul Arrives in Rome
events.description: After wintering on Malta, the party sails through Syracuse, Rhegium, and Puteoli. Roman believers travel out to meet Paul, who enters the capital under guard but is permitted to live in private quarters.

events.title: Paul Addresses Rome's Jewish Leaders
events.description: Paul explains his appeal and innocence to local Jewish leaders, who arrange a fuller hearing. Some accept his scriptural case for Jesus while others reject it, and Paul declares that Gentiles will receive the message.

events.title: Paul Teaches Freely under Guard in Rome
events.description: For two years Paul supports his own lodging and welcomes everyone who visits him. Though still in custody, he openly proclaims God's kingdom and teaches about Jesus without hindrance.
